:::{#def-surv-fn}
#### Survival function

The **survival function** (or **survivor function**)
of a random variable $T$,
denoted $\surv(t)$,
is the probability that $T$ exceeds $t$:

$$\surv(t) \eqdef \Pr(T > t)$$

:::

::: notes

The name comes from time-to-event analysis:
if $T$ is the time at which a participant dies,
then $\surv(t)$ is the probability that the participant is still alive at time $t$.
The definition itself applies to any random variable.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#thm-survival-expressions-1}
#### Survival function and CDF

For any random variable $T$ with [CDF](#def-cdf) $F(t)$:

$$\surv(t) = 1 - F(t)$$

If $T$ is continuous with [density](#def-pdf) $f(t)$, then also:

$$\surv(t) = \int_{u=t}^{\infty} f(u)\,du$$

:::

::: proof

The event $\{T > t\}$ is the complement of the event $\{T \le t\}$,
so the [complement rule](probability-basics.qmd#cor-p-neg0) gives:

$$
\ba
\surv(t)
&\eqdef \Pr(T > t)
&& \text{(definition of the survival function)} \\
&= 1 - \Pr(T \le t)
&& \text{(complement rule)} \\
&= 1 - F(t)
&& \text{(definition of the CDF)}
\ea
$$

For continuous $T$, the density integrates to 1 over the real line
(@thm-density-sums-to-one),
and $F$ is the integral of the density up to $t$ (@thm-density-vs-CDF), so:

$$
\ba
1 - F(t)
&= \int_{u=-\infty}^{\infty} f(u)\,du - \int_{u=-\infty}^{t} f(u)\,du
&& \text{(total integral is 1; } F \text{ is the integral of } f \text{)} \\
&= \int_{u=t}^{\infty} f(u)\,du
&& \text{(split the first integral at } t \text{ and cancel)}
\ea
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-exp-survfn}
#### Survival function of an exponential distribution

Let $T$ be exponential with rate $\lambda > 0$ (@def-exponential),
so $T$ has density $f(t) = \lambda \ef{-\lambda t}$ for $t \ge 0$.
For $t \ge 0$, by @thm-survival-expressions-1:

$$
\ba
\surv(t)
&= \int_{u=t}^{\infty} \lambda \ef{-\lambda u}\,du
&& \text{(integral form of the survival function)} \\
&= \sb{-\ef{-\lambda u}}_{u=t}^{\infty}
&& \text{(antiderivative of } \lambda \ef{-\lambda u} \text{)} \\
&= 0 - \paren{-\ef{-\lambda t}}
&& \text{(evaluate at the bounds; } \ef{-\lambda u} \to 0 \text{ as } u \to \infty \text{)} \\
&= \ef{-\lambda t}
&& \text{(simplify)}
\ea
$$

For $t < 0$, $\surv(t) = \Pr(T > t) = 1$, since $T \ge 0$.
With $\lambda = 0.5$, for example, $\surv(2) = \ef{-1} \approx 0.368$.

:::
